title: AISAT — Agentic AI Saksham (Tech)
subtitle: Engineering CS Benchmark & Evaluation Assessment
instructions: This is a snapshot of where you actually stand with agentic AI tools right now, not a pass/fail test.
There are 40 questions across five short sections, each with its own instructions.
Answer honestly and move at your own pace.
Your responses are automatically saved in real time.
No trick questions; select the response that best reflects sound technical judgment.

sections.title: Section A · Knowledge Check
sections.description: These questions test whether the concepts from the workshop actually hold up, not whether you remember a definition. Some options will look close together on purpose.

sections.title: Section B · Scenario Judgment
sections.description: Each scenario is a realistic situation, not a trivia question. There's rarely a purely 'correct' answer here — pick the response that reflects the soundest judgment call.

sections.title: Section C · Code Review
sections.description: These are short written answers, not multiple choice. We're checking whether you can spot what's wrong in a real RAG setup and explain the fix in your own words.

sections.title: Section D · Workflow Critique
sections.description: Below is a real execution log from an agent handling a supplier update task. Something in it went wrong. The same transcript stays visible for all four questions in this section.

sections.title: Section E · Tool Depth
sections.description: These are tailored to the tool categories you rated yourself highest on earlier. They test the difference between having used a tool and actually knowing where it breaks.

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q1
questions.prompt: An agent is given a goal and a set of tools, but no explicit step-by-step instructions. What primarily determines the sequence of actions it takes?

options.text: The order the tools are listed in its configuration
The agent's own reasoning loop, deciding each next action based on the goal and prior results
A fixed script the developer writes for every possible goal
The order in which the tools were most recently used

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q2
questions.prompt: Which of these best distinguishes an "agent" from a simple LLM pipeline?

options.text: An agent uses a larger underlying model than a pipeline does
An agent can decide which tool to call next based on intermediate results, a pipeline follows a fixed sequence
An agent never requires any human oversight once launched
An agent only works with structured data, a pipeline works with any input

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q3
questions.prompt: An agent is looping repeatedly on the same failed tool call without making progress. What is the most likely underlying cause?

options.text: The model's context window is too large for the task
The agent has no termination or retry-limit condition, so it keeps retrying on failure
The tool being called is written in the wrong programming language
The agent's temperature setting is set too low

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q4
questions.prompt: When designing an agent that can take real-world actions (sending emails, modifying files), which safeguard matters most before deployment?

options.text: Making sure the agent's prompts are as short as possible
Requiring human confirmation or a permission boundary before irreversible actions
Increasing the model's temperature so it explores more options
Removing all tool-use logging to reduce latency

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q5
questions.prompt: In a multi-step automated workflow, what is the main advantage of breaking a task into discrete steps rather than one large prompt?

options.text: It always makes the workflow run faster
Each step can be checked, retried, or corrected independently if something goes wrong
It reduces the total number of tokens used to zero
It removes the need for any error handling

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q6
questions.prompt: A workflow automation tool triggers an action whenever a new row is added to a spreadsheet. What is this trigger-action pattern generally called?

options.text: A batch process
An event-driven automation
A static pipeline
A manual override

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q7
questions.prompt: A workflow has five sequential steps. Step 3 fails intermittently. What is the most robust design choice?

options.text: Remove step 3 entirely since it's unreliable
Add retry logic and a fallback path specifically around step 3, not the whole workflow
Restart the entire five-step workflow from step 1 every time step 3 fails
Run step 3 last instead of third

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q8
questions.prompt: Why might a workflow that worked correctly in testing fail once deployed with real data?

options.text: Real data often contains edge cases and formatting the test data didn't cover
Deployed workflows always run slower than test workflows
Production environments cannot run automated workflows
The workflow logic changes automatically after deployment

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q9
questions.prompt: When an API call fails with a rate-limit error, what does that typically mean?

options.text: The API key is invalid
Too many requests were sent in a given time window
The request body was formatted incorrectly
The server hosting the API is permanently down

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q10
questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of an API key or token in most integrations?

options.text: To compress the data being sent
To authenticate the request and identify who is making it
To translate the request into a different programming language
To determine which server region handles the request

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q11
questions.prompt: An integration receives a malformed or unexpected response from an external API. What is the best practice?

options.text: Assume the response is correct and proceed
Validate and handle the response explicitly, with a defined fallback if it's malformed
Restart the entire application
Ignore the response and retry the exact same request indefinitely

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q12
questions.prompt: What does MCP (Model Context Protocol) primarily standardize?

options.text: The pricing structure across different AI model providers
How an AI model connects to and uses external tools and data sources
The programming language used to train large language models
The visual interface for chat-based AI applications

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q13
questions.prompt: Why can a large language model state an incorrect fact with the same confident tone as a correct one?

options.text: It intentionally hides uncertainty from users
It generates the most statistically likely next words, which doesn't guarantee factual accuracy
It only makes mistakes on topics after its training cutoff
Confidence in tone is a setting the user must manually enable

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q14
questions.prompt: What does a model's "context window" refer to?

options.text: The visual size of the chat interface
The amount of text the model can consider at once when generating a response
The time period the model was trained on
The number of tools the model can call in one turn

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q15
questions.prompt: Which prompt is most likely to produce a consistent, usable output on the first try?

options.text: "Write something about our project"
"Summarize this report in 3 bullet points, under 20 words each, for a non-technical manager"
"Can you help with this document please"
"Make this better"

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q16
questions.prompt: A prompt keeps producing outputs that are technically correct but in the wrong format for downstream use. What's the most effective fix?

options.text: Increase the model's temperature setting
Explicitly specify the required output format and structure in the prompt itself
Repeat the same prompt multiple times until it works
Switch to a different, unrelated task

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q17
questions.prompt: An AI assistant cites a statistic without a source. What is the appropriate next step?

options.text: Use it as given, since the AI generated it
Trace it back to a verifiable original source before relying on it
Assume it's correct if it sounds plausible
Rephrase it in your own words to avoid needing a source

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q18
questions.prompt: When would a deep-research or multi-source tool mode be necessary instead of a single prompt?

options.text: When the answer requires synthesizing and cross-checking many current sources, not just one
When the task is purely creative writing with no factual claims
Never, a single well-written prompt is always sufficient
Only when the user has no internet access

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q19
questions.prompt: An AI coding assistant is given access to a production database to "help debug faster." What is the main risk?

options.text: The assistant will run slower with more access
It may take unintended or destructive actions beyond what's actually needed for debugging
Production databases cannot be accessed by AI tools at all
The assistant will refuse the task automatically

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q20
questions.prompt: Why is granting an AI agent the minimum necessary permissions (rather than broad access) considered good practice?

options.text: It makes the agent respond faster
It limits the damage if the agent makes an error or is misused
It is required by every AI provider's terms of service
It has no real effect on safety, only on cost

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q21
questions.prompt: An AI agent reports that a multi-step task "completed successfully." Should this be trusted without verification?

options.text: Yes, agents only report success when every step genuinely succeeded
Not necessarily, intermediate steps can fail silently even when the final report says success
Yes, but only for tasks involving text generation
No AI agent can ever report success accurately

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q22
questions.prompt: Which is the strongest signal that AI-generated output needs closer scrutiny before use?

options.text: The output is longer than expected
The output makes a specific, checkable factual or numerical claim
The output took longer than usual to generate
The output uses formal language

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q23
questions.prompt: When using AI to draft a professional email, what should the user still do before sending it?

options.text: Nothing, well-formatted AI output is ready to send as-is
Review it for tone, accuracy, and appropriateness to the actual recipient
Only check the spelling
Make it longer to sound more thorough

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q24
questions.prompt: An AI tool generates a graphic for a presentation. What is the most important thing to check before using it?

options.text: That it matches the intended message and brand context, not just that it looks polished
That it was generated in under 10 seconds
That it uses as many colors as possible
That the AI tool used is the newest version available

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q25
questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of using AI to organize and summarize notes across multiple documents?

options.text: It permanently deletes the original documents
It can surface patterns and connections faster than manual review, though it should still be checked
It guarantees zero factual errors
It replaces the need to read source documents ever again

questions.title: Knowledge Check · Q26
questions.prompt: An AI tool analyzes a dataset and recommends a decision. What should happen before acting on that recommendation?

options.text: Act on it immediately since AI analysis is objective
Sanity-check the underlying data and reasoning, since AI can misread patterns or outliers
Ignore it entirely, AI should never be used for data analysis
Only check the recommendation if the dataset is very large

questions.title: Scenario Judgment · Q1
questions.prompt: You built an agent to process 50 customer records and update a CRM. It reports "all 50 records updated successfully." What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Move on, the agent's report is sufficient confirmation
Spot-check a sample of the records directly in the CRM to confirm the updates are correct
Re-run the entire agent from scratch just to be safe
Ask the agent to repeat its report in different words

questions.title: Scenario Judgment · Q2
questions.prompt: You're automating a workflow that must run reliably every day versus one that can tolerate occasional manual review. Which approach fits a task where a wrong output could cause real financial harm (e.g., auto-approving refunds)?

options.text: Fully automate with no human checkpoint, to maximize speed
Automate the analysis but require human sign-off before the irreversible action executes
Avoid automation entirely and do the task manually forever
Automate it and check results once a month

questions.title: Scenario Judgment · Q3
questions.prompt: An agent meant to research and summarize competitor pricing keeps returning outdated information. Tool access looks correctly configured. What's the most likely root cause to investigate first?

options.text: The agent's summarization style is too concise
The agent may be relying on the model's training data instead of actually calling its search/retrieval tool
The competitor's pricing page uses too many images
The agent needs a longer system prompt

questions.title: Scenario Judgment · Q4
questions.prompt: A team wants to give their support agent access to a tool that can issue account refunds automatically, to "save time." What's the most responsible design?

options.text: Grant full refund authority immediately, since it saves the most time
Have the agent draft the refund for human approval below a set threshold, and require approval above it
Never allow the agent to touch refunds under any circumstance
Grant access but disable all logging so it runs faster

questions.title: Scenario Judgment · Q5
questions.prompt: A team wants to connect an internal tool to an AI assistant so it can pull live inventory data. Before building a custom integration, what should they check first?

options.text: Whether an existing, well-supported connector or MCP server already covers this need
Whether the AI model itself has memorized their inventory numbers
Whether the task can be done without any data at all
Whether the integration will look impressive in a demo

questions.title: Code Review · Q1
questions.prompt: What's likely wrong with this chunking setup, and what would you change?
questions.context: A RAG pipeline splits documents into 2,000-token chunks with no overlap before embedding them. A user asks a question whose answer spans the boundary between two chunks, and the system fails to retrieve it correctly.
questions.explanationHint: RAG chunking · AI Evaluation & Critical Judgement

questions.title: Code Review · Q2
questions.prompt: Why would this cause poor retrieval results, and what's the fix?
questions.context: A team builds a RAG system where documents are embedded using one embedding model, but user queries at inference time are embedded using a different, unrelated embedding model.
questions.explanationHint: Embedding mismatch · AI Research & Info Retrieval

questions.title: Workflow Critique · Q1
questions.prompt: What went wrong in this execution? Identify the flaw.
questions.transcript:
[Agent] Goal: Read latest supplier email, extract new pricing, update spreadsheet.
[Tool Call 1] read_email(folder="Suppliers", limit=1) → returned email from "supplier-updates@vendor-mail.co"
[Agent] Extracted: Item A: ₹450, Item B: ₹1,200, Item C: ₹80
[Tool Call 2] update_spreadsheet(sheet="Pricing", rows=[A,B,C]) → success
[Agent] Task completed successfully. Spreadsheet updated with 3 new prices.

Note: the known supplier domain is "vendor-mail.com" — the email above came from a lookalike
domain, and the agent had permission to write directly to the live pricing sheet with no review step.

questions.title: Tool Depth · Q1
questions.prompt: You need to analyze 40 pages across 6 documents and produce a synthesized comparison. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Paste all 6 documents into a single prompt and ask for a summary
Use the assistant's dedicated multi-document or deep-research mode designed for cross-source synthesis
Summarize each document in a separate, unrelated conversation
Ask the assistant to guess the content without uploading anything

questions.title: Tool Depth · Q2
questions.prompt: An AI coding assistant confidently suggests a library function that doesn't actually exist in the library's current version. What is this failure mode generally called, and what should a developer do before using suggested code?

options.text: This is called "rate limiting" — restart the tool and try again
This is a hallucination — verify the function exists in the actual library documentation before using it
This means the library is broken — switch to a different library entirely
This only happens with very old libraries, so no verification is needed for current ones

questions.title: Tool Depth · Q3
questions.prompt: You're setting up an agent to handle a recurring task with real consequences (e.g., customer communication). What's the best-practice way to use the platform's advanced features here, beyond just giving it a goal and letting it run?

options.text: Give it the broadest possible tool access so it never gets stuck
Configure explicit guardrails, permission scopes, and logging/review checkpoints appropriate to the task's risk
Disable all logging to keep the agent running faster
Avoid using any advanced configuration, since defaults are always safest

questions.explanationHint: Best-practice usage · AI Agents & Digital Workers
